metadata.title: llama-ai and pinned CachyLlama feature inventory
metadata.method: Commit-pinned static source inspection. No binaries were built or executed; hardware performance claims are reported only as repository evidence.

maturity_scale.M0: Documented, dead, duplicate, or unbuilt path.
maturity_scale.M1: Prototype/integrated path with material correctness, security, observability, or validation gaps.
maturity_scale.M2: Operational source path with active churn, recent fixes, or incomplete focused tests.
maturity_scale.M3: Integrated path with focused tests or repeated operational evidence; may still be explicitly experimental.
maturity_scale.M4: Stable, released, compatibility-governed feature. No custom feature in this assessment qualifies.

decision_scale.RETAIN: Preserve the capability or target-native implementation with limited reconciliation.
decision_scale.REDESIGN: Keep the user outcome but rework architecture, security, durability, licensing, or integration.
decision_scale.REJECT: Do not import the pinned implementation or behavior.

features.behavior: Reopens a configured cache root, scans stored checkpoints, and rebuilds the index so target sequence state can be reused after server restart.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX has disk prompt-cache spill, but its owned namespace is deliberately removed on shutdown.
features.rationale: Add an explicit persistent mode to the existing ROCmFPX cache engine rather than replacing its tested run-scoped mode.
features.risks: Crash consistency, stale format detection, tenant confidentiality, and restart index integrity.

features.behavior: Classifies checkpoints by recency and moves them through hot, warm, and cold tiers after turns.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX currently has RAM plus bounded disk entries, not the same three-tier policy.
features.rationale: Preserve the policy objective but implement one budgeted cache with explicit residency state, pressure feedback, and testable promotion/demotion.
features.risks: Source defaults and parent overrides disagree; auto budgeting is not cgroup-aware.

features.behavior: Stores target-model state, optional draft-model state, and speculative-decoder metadata as one logical checkpoint.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX already persists target/draft pairs and stateful MTP metadata.
features.rationale: Unify record metadata and validation with ROCmFPX's existing target/draft/state_spec representation.
features.risks: Partial component restores must never be treated as a complete hit.

features.behavior: Reads and writes large state blobs in 64 MiB chunks instead of requiring a single giant host operation.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX has robust file commit handling but can reuse a bounded transfer helper where its serialization path benefits.
features.rationale: Port the chunk-loop concept behind the target's current I/O abstraction and preserve its fault injection.
features.risks: Short reads/writes and cancellation paths require tests.

features.behavior: Can force checkpoint data to stable storage unless no-fsync is selected.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX already flushes files and directories in its tested commit path.
features.rationale: Represent durability as an explicit strict/relaxed policy and retain ROCmFPX's atomic pair commit.
features.risks: CachyLlama writes directly to final names, so fsync alone does not make metadata publication atomic.

features.behavior: Rejects state whose model/cache compatibility hash differs from the active context.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX already validates state shape and file integrity but needs a stable restart-persistence namespace key.
features.rationale: Define a versioned fingerprint covering model identity, context layout, KV types, backend-relevant serialization version, and draft/MTP shape.
features.risks: Under-specified fingerprints can load semantically incompatible state.

features.behavior: Persists a bounded token prefix with checkpoint metadata for restart-time prefix matching.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX's in-memory disk index already tracks complete prompt token vectors for the current run.
features.rationale: Persist a compact, versioned token index or manifest in persistent mode; verify candidate tokens against the loaded file before accepting.
features.risks: A 4096-token metadata prefix cannot prove equality for longer prompts by itself.

features.behavior: Bounds the number of cold checkpoints and evicts old entries from a cold ring.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX already enforces a byte limit and LRU eviction.
features.rationale: Retain count as a secondary guard only; use byte quotas as the primary policy.
features.risks: Count-only limits behave poorly across models with very different state sizes.

features.behavior: Derives tier capacities from reported free RAM and allocates most of the calculated budget to the hot tier.
dependencies: Linux sysinfo or platform memory query
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX already has an explicit RAM cache limit.
features.rationale: Keep explicit limits authoritative; optional auto mode must use MemAvailable/cgroup limits and reserve headroom for model/runtime pressure.
features.risks: Current free-RAM calculation can overcommit and is not container-aware.

features.behavior: Issues read-ahead hints for a likely checkpoint before the restore is required.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX has no documented persistent prefetch layer.
features.rationale: Add as an optional optimization after correctness and persistence land; measure hit rate and I/O amplification.
features.risks: Prefetch may evict useful page cache or waste I/O on low-confidence candidates.

features.behavior: Places explicit-user caches under a user-oriented namespace distinct from anonymous conversation roots.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX's current run directory is process-private, not tenant-addressed.
features.rationale: Use an authenticated tenant ID and opaque keyed hash in the path; never trust a request field as the authorization boundary.
features.risks: Path disclosure, user-supplied identity spoofing, and owner-wide file permissions.

features.behavior: Creates cache directories and state files using conventional shared-readable modes in the component path.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX's existing disk cache uses owner-only namespaces and files.
features.rationale: Do not import CachyLlama's permission choices; keep ROCmFPX's 0700/0600 posture and add optional encryption for persistent multi-tenant use.
features.risks: Prompts and hidden reasoning can be secrets.

features.behavior: Writes checkpoint payloads directly to their final paths and removes them on detected failure.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX already uses temporary files, atomic rename, and directory synchronization.
features.rationale: Keep the target's commit protocol; persistent mode should add a manifest transaction rather than regress to direct publication.
features.risks: Power loss can leave a final-name partial file.

features.behavior: Centralizes open, pread, pwrite, fsync, unlink, and advisory behavior.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX supports cross-platform server builds and has its own filesystem code.
features.rationale: Port only useful abstractions, preserving Windows UTF-8 and fault-injection behavior in the target.
features.risks: A POSIX-named layer is not sufficient for Windows portability.

features.behavior: Scans checkpoint files and restores cache metadata when no live process index exists.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX current entries exist only in process memory and are deleted on exit.
features.rationale: Use a checksummed manifest plus orphan reconciliation; bound startup cost and quarantine malformed entries.
features.risks: Unbounded directory scans and corrupted metadata can delay startup.

features.behavior: Stores a system-prefix sequence state independently of a conversation so requests sharing the same system prompt can skip repeated prefill.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX has general prompt-prefix caching but no separately governed persistent system-prefix store.
features.rationale: Implement as a scoped prefix-cache class in the target engine, keyed by model/template/tenant/system token sequence.
features.risks: Cross-tenant leakage and false boundary detection are high-impact.

features.behavior: Scans sys-{hash}.bin entries and restores their state into an in-memory catalog at startup.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX's cache is run-scoped.
features.rationale: Use the same versioned persistent manifest and atomic commit layer as conversation checkpoints.
features.risks: Startup memory cost scales with stored system entries because state blobs are loaded into RAM.

features.behavior: Expires system cache entries after a configured unused-day limit and evicts LRU entries above a maximum count.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX already has byte-bounded LRU mechanics.
features.rationale: Combine age, byte, and count limits; expose tenant and global quotas.
features.risks: Wall-clock changes and large state variance require conservative accounting.

features.feature: Full-prompt hash plus bounded token prefix
features.behavior: Keys a system entry by a full prompt hash and records a bounded token prefix and compatibility metadata.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX can reuse its token vectors and target/draft validation.
features.rationale: Use a cryptographic or collision-resistant content key over canonical tokens and include template/model/tenant scope.
features.risks: Hash collisions or tokenization drift must fail closed.

features.behavior: Decodes token text and searches for user/human/end-of-generation markers to decide where the reusable system prefix ends.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX supports multiple chat templates and structured request conversion.
features.rationale: Derive the boundary from the parsed message/template AST before tokenization, then verify the exact token range.
features.risks: Heuristics can cache user content as a shared system prefix.

features.behavior: Compares incoming tokens with stored checkpoint prefixes and ranks by longest common prefix, recency, and checkpoint length.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX already performs LCP matching for RAM and disk prompt cache entries.
features.rationale: Consolidate around the target implementation and add restart-persistent index candidates.
features.risks: Minimum acceptance and exact state boundary rules must remain caller-specific.

features.behavior: Requires approximately 90% token-prefix similarity before restoring another conversation's checkpoint.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX prompt caching already matches prefixes within the running server.
features.rationale: Make threshold configurable by scope; require authenticated tenant equality and a minimum absolute token count.
features.risks: A ratio alone is unsafe for short prompts.

features.behavior: Searches anonymous cache directories for a stored prompt that can continue a new conversation.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX does not retain cross-run directories.
features.rationale: Replace global scanning with a manifest/index partitioned by model and authenticated tenant; anonymous reuse should default to process-local only.
features.risks: Cross-user data reuse and unbounded I/O.

features.behavior: Rejects very small continuation comparisons before treating them as a useful session match.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX can apply this in its candidate filter.
features.rationale: Use both minimum absolute tokens and ratio thresholds, with higher requirements for cross-conversation or cross-restart matches.
features.risks: Fixed thresholds may be model/template dependent.

features.behavior: Uses a configurable slot-prompt similarity threshold to choose a warm slot with a reusable prefix.
features.license: MIT for component; GPL-3.0 for parent profile
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX inherits llama.cpp slot prompt reuse.
features.rationale: Keep target behavior; document interaction with persistent cache and user affinity.
features.risks: Affinity and prefix reuse must be evaluated under one authorization-aware selection policy.

features.behavior: Prefetches the selected checkpoint so restore latency can overlap request preparation.
features.target_overlap: No target equivalent was identified.
features.rationale: Add only after persistence and candidate correctness are tested; instrument useful-prefetch ratio.
features.risks: Can amplify SSD writes/reads and page-cache churn.

features.behavior: Creates checkpoints at configured token intervals while processing long prompts.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX already has context checkpoint controls and prompt-cache saves.
features.rationale: Keep target checkpoint scheduling and integrate persistent snapshots as a separate policy.
features.risks: Source and documentation disagree on the minimum/default step; very frequent snapshots can dominate I/O.

features.behavior: Marks a final checkpoint for creation after the first generated token so the restored state has the needed generation boundary.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX has prompt-cache saves at task boundaries.
features.rationale: Preserve the semantic boundary, but express it as an explicit checkpoint reason/state in the target.
features.risks: Ordering bugs can persist a state that cannot resume generation correctly.

features.behavior: Restores target state, optional draft state, and speculative state into a selected slot.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX already stores target/draft and stateful MTP records.
features.rationale: Merge semantics into the target's paired-state validation and exact-boundary rules.
features.risks: A draft/spec mismatch must force safe catch-up or full prefill.

features.behavior: Loads a serialized sequence into the currently assigned server slot rather than assuming the source slot ID.
features.target_overlap: The target uses per-slot sequence state APIs.
features.rationale: Keep explicit destination sequence IDs in every restore API and add a regression test based on the historical cold-restore fix.
features.risks: Implicit source IDs can restore into the wrong sequence.

features.behavior: Clears attention KV state while preserving recurrent state for hybrid/recurrent models.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX includes MTP and evolving recurrent/hybrid support.
features.rationale: Retain the primitive only if the target base does not already contain an equivalent; validate per architecture.
features.risks: Incorrect partial clearing can silently corrupt recurrent continuation.

features.behavior: Exposes named slot-state files through an HTTP action route when a slot-save path is configured.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX inherits the slot-state API family.
features.rationale: Keep the endpoint but enforce owner-only directories, API authorization, quotas, and audit logs.
features.risks: Named files are an administrative surface separate from automatic cache persistence.

features.behavior: Treats failed or incomplete restores as misses and continues through normal prompt processing.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX tests corruption and partial target/draft pairs.
features.rationale: Use the target's stricter file-size/pair validation and circuit-breaker semantics.
features.risks: Fallback must clear any partially applied sequence state.

features.behavior: Maintains reusable prompt states in RAM in addition to SSD-backed checkpoints.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX already has a byte-bounded RAM prompt cache.
features.rationale: Keep the target implementation as the first tier; persistent disk should be a lower tier.
features.risks: RAM accounting must include target, draft, and metadata.

features.behavior: Can reuse sufficiently large prompt chunks via KV shifting under the server cache-reuse setting.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX already documents and carries cache-reuse behavior.
features.rationale: Retain target-native behavior; test interactions with loaded persistent state and hybrid memory.
features.risks: Not all memory types support arbitrary shifting.

features.behavior: Accepts llama_user_id in OpenAI-style request bodies and propagates it to task scheduling.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX has OpenAI-compatible endpoints but no verified authenticated tenant cache scope.
features.rationale: Accept a user hint only behind a trusted gateway; bind an internal tenant principal from API-key/JWT context.
features.risks: Client-supplied identity is spoofable.

features.behavior: Maps metadata.user_id from Anthropic-style requests into the same scheduling identity field.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX may retain Anthropic compatibility from its llama.cpp base.
features.rationale: Keep protocol parsing as a hint, then map through the same authenticated principal layer as OpenAI requests.
features.risks: Protocol parity must not create different authorization rules.

features.behavior: Validates length and allowed characters before using an identifier in scheduling or filesystem namespace selection.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX should validate any external label before logging or lookup.
features.rationale: Retain strict syntax validation but store a keyed hash/opaque internal ID instead of the raw value.
features.risks: Validation prevents traversal but not identity spoofing.

features.behavior: Rejects or defers requests when a non-empty user identity reaches the configured in-flight limit.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX has global slot limits but no assessed tenant quota.
features.rationale: Implement one authoritative scheduler quota keyed by authenticated tenant, with atomic admission and release.
features.risks: Pinned code duplicates checks at HTTP and allocator layers; races and accounting drift are possible.

features.behavior: Documentation describes a shared anonymous bucket, but the pinned code explicitly exempts empty user IDs from per-user accounting.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX should not inherit the contradiction.
features.rationale: Define an explicit unauthenticated/global policy; production multi-tenant deployments should require authentication.
features.risks: Anonymous traffic can consume all global slots.

features.behavior: Prefers a least-recently-used slot previously associated with the same user to improve reuse.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX already chooses slots using prompt similarity and availability.
features.rationale: Combine authorization, user affinity, and prefix score in a single eligibility/ranking pass; never select cross-tenant state.
features.risks: Separate selection passes can accidentally prioritize prefix reuse before isolation.

features.behavior: Creates persistent cache wrappers and paths under a user namespace.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX has private process directories, not persistent tenant namespaces.
features.rationale: Namespace by authenticated tenant hash and model fingerprint, with per-tenant owner/key policy.
features.risks: Raw IDs in paths leak identity and allow spoofed cache access.

features.behavior: The architecture has user cache maps, but pinned get_stats aggregation omits them.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX has cache counters but no assessed per-tenant view.
features.rationale: Do not port the omission; define aggregate and tenant-scoped metrics with cardinality controls.
features.risks: Operational dashboards would underreport persistent usage.

features.feature: Per-user tier aging on turn completion
features.behavior: The pinned turn-completion path advances anonymous caches but omits user cache wrappers.
features.target_overlap: No direct target equivalent.
features.rationale: Centralize all cache instances in one registry and iterate one lifecycle interface.
features.risks: User entries can remain hot indefinitely or avoid intended eviction.

features.behavior: Logs scheduling/rate-limit decisions with the unredacted user identifier.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX logs are shared operational output.
features.rationale: Log a stable keyed pseudonym, not raw identity; keep raw values out of metrics labels.
features.risks: PII/secrets leakage and high-cardinality observability.

features.feature: Identity as routing metadata, not authentication
features.behavior: The user identifier is accepted from the request body and is not itself a credential or verified principal.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX supports API keys/TLS but needs explicit identity binding.
features.rationale: Resolve tenant identity in authenticated middleware and ignore/validate client hints according to gateway policy.
features.risks: Using body metadata as a security boundary enables cache theft.

features.feature: Unified cache and slot ownership lifecycle
features.behavior: Ownership state is currently distributed across task parsing, slot counters, slot user fields, and separate page-manager maps.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX has its own scheduler and cache engine.
features.rationale: Introduce one TenantContext/CacheScope object passed through admission, selection, restore, save, metrics, and release.
features.risks: Distributed accounting is difficult to audit and test.

features.feature: SSD cache CLI and environment controls
features.behavior: Exposes path, tier windows/budgets, checkpoint limits, system-prompt limits, retention, fsync, and concurrency settings.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX currently exposes --cache-disk and --cache-disk-limit.
features.rationale: Extend target-native naming with explicit persistent-mode, durability, retention, and namespace controls; preserve backward compatibility.
features.risks: Cachy source, docs, and parent runner use conflicting defaults.

features.behavior: llama-ai supplies operational defaults that differ from component defaults and selects cache use by model/hardware profile.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX has build/run scripts but should not directly import GPL shell code into its MIT tree.
features.rationale: Re-express useful profile rules in an MIT-compatible configuration layer or external GPL deployment project.
features.risks: License incompatibility for direct incorporation; default drift.

features.behavior: Prunes cache entries not used within a configured number of days.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX currently evicts by byte pressure and run lifetime.
features.rationale: Add optional age eviction to persistent mode with monotonic/validated timestamps and dry-run reporting.
features.risks: Clock rollback and unreadable metadata.

features.behavior: Deletes an old conversation cache directory when the configured conversation limit is reached.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX uses byte-bounded LRU entries.
features.rationale: Use manifest-backed LRU/bytes per tenant; do not choose victims solely by directory mtime.
features.risks: Separate user/anonymous limits and non-atomic deletion.

features.behavior: Discovers existing persistent entries at startup; malformed or expired entries can be skipped or removed.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX already cleans stale private run directories using ownership markers and locks.
features.rationale: Combine target ownership/lock safety with a persistent manifest, quarantine, bounded reconciliation, and schema migration.
features.risks: Concurrent instances and partial entries need clear ownership.

features.behavior: No dedicated HTTP endpoint for listing, inspecting, pruning, or invalidating automatic SSD cache entries was identified.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX likewise exposes metrics/slots rather than a persistent-cache admin API.
features.rationale: Add authenticated inspect/prune/invalidate endpoints or an offline admin CLI, with tenant scoping and dry-run.
features.risks: Administrative APIs can expose prompt metadata and become a destructive control surface.

features.behavior: Cache internals track hits, misses, bytes, tiers, and restore timing, but complete user-scoped aggregation is not wired into the standard metrics endpoint.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX already tracks disk saves, loads, evictions, failures, and prompt cache hits in logs/timings.
features.rationale: Expose low-cardinality cache counters and gauges from one target cache engine.
features.risks: Metrics cardinality and undercounting.

features.behavior: Compatibility checks cause old state to be rejected when model/cache identity changes.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX model formats and MTP state evolve rapidly.
features.rationale: Retain fail-closed rejection and add explicit invalidate/migrate tooling keyed by exact model fingerprint.
features.risks: Rejected files can consume disk indefinitely without cleanup.

features.behavior: A second hot/warm/cold page-manager implementation includes asynchronous writeback concepts but is not linked into the active common library.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX already has a working prompt cache engine.
features.rationale: Do not port this duplicate path. Extract only independently valuable test ideas after verifying semantics.
features.risks: Unbuilt code, inconsistent size comments/literals, duplicate architecture.

features.behavior: Runs each loaded model in a child llama-server process behind a router and proxies requests to the selected child.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX inherits modern llama.cpp router capabilities or can reconcile against them.
features.rationale: Retain upstream/target router implementation rather than transplanting an older fork copy.
features.risks: Router mode is explicitly experimental and unsuitable for untrusted direct exposure.

features.behavior: Exposes explicit model load and unload operations through JSON endpoints.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX's current base may already contain equivalent model routes.
features.rationale: Use target-native routes and apply authentication, authorization, resource quotas, and audit logging.
features.risks: Loading arbitrary presets can execute resource-heavy or unsafe configurations.

features.feature: Model autoload on first routed request
features.behavior: Optionally starts an unloaded configured model when a request names it.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX documents model router controls in its inherited server.
features.rationale: Retain behind an explicit policy and admission controller.
features.risks: Cold-start latency and denial-of-service by model thrashing.

features.feature: Maximum loaded-model count with LRU unload
features.behavior: Caps active child models and unloads the least recently used model before loading another.
features.target_overlap: Applicable to ROCmFPX where large quantized models compete for UMA/VRAM.
features.rationale: Retain target-native LRU but make memory pressure and pinned models first-class inputs.
features.risks: Request-level recency alone may evict an expensive or pinned model.

features.behavior: Reloads model definitions, updates metadata, autoloads newly configured models, and broadcasts a lifecycle event.
features.target_overlap: Useful for ROCmFPX model presets and quant variants.
features.rationale: Retain with schema validation and atomic catalog swap.
features.risks: Partial reloads and stale child parameters.

features.behavior: Loads model presets from cache, a configured models directory, and preset sources.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX users manage many quantized variants.
features.rationale: Keep target-native discovery with explicit trust boundaries and allowlisted roots.
features.risks: Untrusted presets and path traversal.

features.feature: Hugging Face GGUF discovery and split download
features.behavior: The parent launcher resolves repository files and downloads complete or split GGUF artifacts using available Hugging Face tools.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX has its own distribution/build workflows.
features.rationale: Implement or document an MIT-compatible downloader outside the inference core; verify checksums and free space.
features.risks: Directly copying parent shell code would import GPL obligations; remote artifacts are untrusted input.

features.behavior: The parent inspects GGUF metadata to choose dense, MoE, recurrent/SSM, and hardware-specific launch profiles.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX has multiple quant families, backends, MTP paths, and Strix profiles.
features.rationale: Reimplement as a declarative, tested preset resolver in the target or an external deployment package.
features.risks: Heuristic metadata scanning from the first file bytes is brittle.

features.feature: Cache scope tied to model compatibility
features.behavior: Persistent states are accepted only for a compatible model/cache fingerprint, naturally invalidating reuse after incompatible model changes.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX frequently changes quant type and MTP layout.
features.rationale: Namespace cache roots by exact model fingerprint and runtime state ABI, not just human model alias.
features.risks: Aliases can point to different files over time.

features.behavior: Serves OpenAI-compatible chat-completions and completions endpoints, including streaming.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX is built on a newer llama.cpp server.
features.rationale: Keep target-native API behavior and add cache/user extensions through namespaced fields or headers.
features.risks: Compatibility fields evolve; avoid fork-only semantics without versioning.

features.behavior: Converts Responses API requests to chat-completion internals and emits Responses-style events.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX's target base already includes modern response formatting.
features.rationale: Reconcile with target rather than cherry-picking fork code.
features.risks: Event compatibility is sensitive to upstream changes.

features.behavior: Converts Anthropic Messages requests to internal chat completions and returns Anthropic-formatted streaming/non-streaming responses.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX may already carry this upstream surface.
features.rationale: Retain target-native implementation; map metadata.user_id only through trusted identity policy.
features.risks: Protocol conversion can lose unsupported semantics.

features.behavior: Exposes native completion and fill-in-the-middle operations in addition to OpenAI-compatible endpoints.
features.target_overlap: Useful for coding models quantized by ROCmFPX.
features.rationale: Keep target-native support and capability checks.
features.risks: FIM token assumptions are model-specific.

features.behavior: Supports embedding generation and rank-model reranking when the server is started in the corresponding mode.
features.target_overlap: Independent of cache port and likely already present in target.
features.rationale: Retain from target base.
features.risks: Persistent generation-state caching does not apply unchanged to embedding/rank workloads.

features.behavior: Maps supported audio transcription requests through multimodal chat processing.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX model quantization can apply to multimodal-capable models if kernels/types support them.
features.rationale: Keep target-native endpoint; exclude multimodal prompt states from persistent cache until deterministic state identity is defined.
features.risks: Target disk cache explicitly skips multimodal token states.

features.behavior: Provides GET slot status and POST save/restore/erase operations for a selected slot.
features.target_overlap: Likely inherited by ROCmFPX.
features.rationale: Keep with authentication and distinguish manual slot files from automatic persistent cache entries.
features.risks: Manual restore can overwrite active state.

features.behavior: Associates SSE output with a conversation ID and exposes lookup, retrieval, and deletion for reconnecting clients.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX can benefit for long agent outputs independently of KV persistence.
features.rationale: Port only if absent from the target base; bind stream lookup/deletion to authenticated ownership.
features.risks: Conversation IDs can become bearer secrets.

features.behavior: Lists configured models, reports status/presets, loads/unloads models, and streams lifecycle events.
features.target_overlap: Useful for ROCmFPX quant variants.
features.rationale: Use target-native router API with authorization and resource controls.
features.risks: Experimental surface and sensitive preset exposure.

features.behavior: Lists and changes active LoRA adapters without a process restart.
features.target_overlap: Useful to ROCmFPX models and independent of cache implementation.
features.rationale: Keep target-native implementation; include adapter set in cache compatibility fingerprint.
features.risks: Restoring state produced under a different adapter set is invalid.

features.behavior: Registers expert tracking/statistics and control routes for MoE diagnostics and tuning.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX has strong MoE/Strix interest but target instrumentation may differ.
features.rationale: Treat as an optional diagnostic extension; reconcile against target graph/kernel architecture and protect control endpoints.
features.risks: Limited test evidence and potential performance overhead.

features.behavior: Exposes tokenizer conversion and chat-template rendering without running inference.
features.target_overlap: Useful for exact persistent-cache key construction and clients.
features.rationale: Keep target-native endpoints and include template identity in persistent cache keys.
features.risks: Template changes alter token sequences and invalidate state.

features.behavior: Reports health during load/sleep and exposes model/server capability metadata.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX services need health and capability probes.
features.rationale: Keep target-native behavior and add a cache readiness/degraded status field.
features.risks: Health should distinguish serving readiness from process liveness.

features.behavior: Emits prompt/generation counters, throughput, request queue depth, slot utilization, and process start time.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX already supports metrics.
features.rationale: Extend target metrics with persistent cache hits/misses/bytes/restore latency/circuit-breaker state.
features.risks: Do not label by raw user or conversation.

features.behavior: Returns cached prompt-token counts and prompt/generation timing in completion results.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX tests use cache_n and prompt_n reductions as hit evidence.
features.rationale: Keep target response timings and add an optional cache source field such as ram, run-disk, persistent-disk, or system-prefix.
features.risks: Response schema compatibility and information disclosure.

features.behavior: Logs checkpoint saves, restores, evictions, cold starts, and failures.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX already has structured-looking disk cache logs and failure counters.
features.rationale: Normalize target logs with stable event names, byte/token counts, duration, scope pseudonym, and reason codes.
features.risks: Raw paths/identifiers can leak sensitive metadata.

features.behavior: Broadcasts model load, unload, and reload events to connected clients.
features.target_overlap: Useful for orchestration around large ROCmFPX models.
features.rationale: Keep target-native stream with authorization and reconnect semantics.
features.risks: Status data can reveal model inventory.

features.behavior: Exposes expert-selection information for MoE analysis.
features.target_overlap: Potentially valuable for Strix Halo MoE kernel tuning.
features.rationale: Validate overhead and output semantics on target models before enabling.
features.risks: Sparse evidence and endpoint stability.

features.behavior: Internal cache statistics exist, but pinned server aggregation omits user cache maps.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX should expose one authoritative cache engine's counters.
features.rationale: Do not copy the split-map aggregation; centralize metrics in the target cache object.
features.risks: Undercounting makes capacity and hit-rate decisions unreliable.

features.behavior: Builds CachyLlama for Vulkan, ROCm/HIP, or Metal with backend-specific CMake settings.
dependencies: Vulkan SDK or ROCm or Metal
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX already ships dedicated AMD/backend build scripts.
features.rationale: Keep ROCmFPX build scripts; transplant only configuration knowledge through clean-room MIT-compatible changes.
features.risks: Direct script copying would impose GPL obligations.

features.behavior: Runs llama-server as a managed service with restart policy and hardening directives.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX deployments may use systemd but paths/options differ.
features.rationale: Generate a parameterized unit or packaging template from target-supported flags; validate with systemd-analyze.
features.risks: Pinned unit has host-specific paths and option drift.

features.behavior: Force-kills existing llama-server processes and port holders before starting a new server.
features.target_overlap: A shared ROCmFPX host may run multiple independent model services.
features.rationale: Use PID files, systemd/container ownership, graceful shutdown, and a bounded escalation policy.
features.risks: Can kill unrelated tenants or services.

features.behavior: Supports API-key authentication and server TLS certificate/key options.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX inherits server authentication/TLS features.
features.rationale: Keep target-native implementation and use authenticated principal context for cache tenant binding.
features.risks: Static API keys need rotation and must not appear in presets/status output.

features.behavior: Selects local models or downloads Hugging Face GGUF files before launch.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX models are distributed as GGUF variants and may be split.
features.rationale: Provide a separate, checksummed provisioning command or documented workflow under compatible licensing.
features.risks: Supply-chain integrity and partial downloads.

features.behavior: Maps AMD PCI/device information to gfx targets, HSA overrides, memory tiers, and recommended profiles.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX already has device-specific build scripts but benefits from runtime guidance.
features.rationale: Move stable detection into an MIT-compatible capability probe with explicit overrides and tests.
features.risks: Device IDs and driver behavior evolve.

features.behavior: Can use amd-smi or mutate systemd-boot/GRUB kernel parameters to expand GPU-accessible memory.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX documents UMA settings but should not own host boot configuration.
features.rationale: Document validated host settings and provide a separate opt-in administrator tool, not part of the inference package.
features.risks: Boot failure, over-allocation, portability, and privilege escalation.

features.behavior: Component source defaults, server documentation, and parent profile overrides form three configuration layers.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX already has its own CLI defaults.
features.rationale: Publish one generated schema and precedence table; make profile overrides explicit and machine-readable.
features.risks: Current values conflict, including hot window, cold count, and checkpoint-step documentation.

features.behavior: The inference component is MIT, while the parent launch/build/deployment layer is GPL-3.0 and its documentation has a separate content license.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX is MIT.
features.rationale: Port MIT component code with notices; clean-room reimplement parent behavior or keep it as a separate GPL work.
features.risks: Combining GPL parent code into the MIT target changes distribution obligations.

features.behavior: Recognizes Strix Halo gfx1151 in deployment and HIP architecture classification.
features.license: Mixed: GPL parent detection, MIT backend
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX explicitly targets Strix Halo and already carries RDNA3.5 support.
features.rationale: Use target-native detection; reconcile only missing device IDs or capability probes.
features.risks: Hard-coded HSA overrides can hide real compiler/runtime incompatibility.

features.behavior: Exports an HSA gfx override and unified-memory settings for Strix Halo ROCm execution.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX quick start already documents HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION and unified memory.
features.rationale: Keep target-documented environment and add version-gated validation rather than copying shell code.
features.risks: Overrides vary by ROCm release.

features.behavior: Chooses large contexts and may disable SSD checkpointing for selected dense/MoE Halo profiles because UMA can hold state in memory.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX targets the same APU and often runs large MoE models.
features.rationale: Convert to a declarative memory estimator based on model/KV/context/parallelism, retaining SSD as an explicit resilience option.
features.risks: Static profiles can exceed memory or disable useful restart persistence.

features.behavior: Uses RDNA3.5-specific warp choices for quantized matrix-vector generation paths.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX has newer custom ROCmFPX kernel formats and target-specific tuning.
features.rationale: Benchmark-port individual launch heuristics per ROCmFPX type; do not wholesale replace target kernels.
features.risks: Tuning for Q/K/IQ types may not transfer to ROCmFPX formats.

features.behavior: Selects a larger warp count for a narrow recurrent gated-delta-net shape on RDNA3.5.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX includes MTP and may host recurrent/hybrid models.
features.rationale: Cherry-pick concept only after target-side correctness and end-to-end model benchmarks.
features.risks: Shape-specific tuning can regress other models.

features.behavior: Classifies AMD Vulkan devices using subgroup and integer-dot capabilities to select architecture-specific paths.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX recommends Vulkan for several tested Strix decode workloads and has newer Vulkan kernels.
features.rationale: Keep target-native implementation; reconcile any missing capability logic narrowly.
features.risks: Capability inference can conflate RDNA generations.

features.behavior: Counts all memory heaps for integrated GPUs rather than only device-local heaps when reporting capacity.
features.target_overlap: Directly relevant to Strix Halo UMA and likely present in the newer target.
features.rationale: Retain target implementation and add pressure-aware reservations rather than treating all UMA as available.
features.risks: Reported budget is not equivalent to safe allocatable memory.

features.feature: Vulkan graph reordering and fusion preservation
features.behavior: Reorders graph nodes around MoE, normalization, recurrent, and view patterns to improve execution while preserving dependencies.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX has a newer Vulkan backend with ROCmFPX-specific shaders.
features.rationale: Diff at symbol level and port only missing optimizer cases with backend-op correctness tests.
features.risks: Large backend files have high merge-conflict and regression risk.

features.behavior: Records exact environment, canary models, correctness totals, benchmark commands, and rejected kernel experiments.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX already publishes Strix/MTP benchmarks and experimental status.
features.rationale: Retain the engineering practice: every kernel change needs correctness gates, matched baselines, and a rejection record.
features.risks: Notes mix clean commits and dirty local builds; provenance must be normalized.

features.behavior: Local evidence favors Vulkan over HIP for selected Strix Halo decode workloads, while both backends are supported.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX independently reports Vulkan as the tested decode starting point on Strix Halo.
features.rationale: Keep backend choice workload-driven and benchmark both for each format/model.
features.risks: Results are hardware, driver, model, context, and quant dependent.

features.behavior: Prioritizes MoE throughput and uses Qwen/GPT-OSS canaries while accepting some dense-model tradeoffs when correctness is intact.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX has strong MoE and agent-format focus.
features.rationale: Separate kernel/profile presets by workload rather than one global Strix default.
features.risks: A MoE-biased default can regress dense models.

features.behavior: ROCmFPX already spills prompt state to a private, byte-bounded disk namespace for the current server run.
features.target_overlap: This is the target implementation.
features.rationale: Keep as the default non-persistent mode and extend rather than replace it.
features.risks: Not reusable after clean restart by design.

features.behavior: Writes target and optional draft state through temporary files, validates size, flushes, renames atomically, and syncs the directory.
features.target_overlap: This is the strongest persistence primitive in the target.
features.rationale: Use it as the foundation for persistent CachyLlama-style checkpoints.
features.risks: Manifest publication must be made equally atomic.

features.behavior: Disables further disk saves after an I/O failure while preserving safe fallback behavior and accounting.
features.target_overlap: This is the target implementation.
features.rationale: Preserve for persistent mode and expose breaker state in metrics/health.
features.risks: A permanent breaker may require an administrative reset or retry policy.

features.behavior: Tests hits, LRU, target/draft pairs, corruption, failure handling, cleanup, and accounting.
features.target_overlap: This is target validation infrastructure.
features.rationale: Extend it with restart persistence, manifest corruption, tenant isolation, concurrent instances, and upgrade tests.
features.risks: Hardware-independent tests do not replace live ROCm/Vulkan validation.

features.behavior: Treats stateful MTP cache records as exact-token-boundary entries while allowing ordinary stateless prefixes to subsume shorter entries.
features.target_overlap: This is target behavior.
features.rationale: Preserve when adding persistence and system-prefix caching.
features.risks: Relaxing exact-boundary rules can restore invalid speculative state.

features.feature: Strix Halo ROCmFPX and MTP baseline
features.behavior: Already supplies Strix Halo build scripts, HIP/Vulkan paths, ROCmFPX quants, MTP execution, and published local validation.
features.target_overlap: This is the target baseline.
features.rationale: Port server/cache capabilities without overwriting newer quant/backend/MTP work.
features.risks: The target is explicitly experimental and performance is workload-specific.

features.behavior: Can expose read, search, write, edit, diff, time, and shell-execution tools through /tools.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX is an inference/quant target and should not couple privileged host tools to its public model server.
features.rationale: Keep disabled; place tools in a separately sandboxed, authenticated agent runtime if needed.
features.risks: Remote code execution and filesystem disclosure.

features.behavior: Can expose a Web UI CORS proxy for MCP integrations.
features.target_overlap: No cache-port dependency and high exposure risk.
features.rationale: Do not enable in ROCmFPX's inference server; use a dedicated, allowlisted reverse proxy.
features.risks: SSRF, credential forwarding, and trust-boundary collapse.

features.behavior: Registers compatibility handling for Google Cloud Platform serving conventions.
features.target_overlap: May already exist in the target's newer llama.cpp server.
features.rationale: Retain target-native implementation if required by deployments.
features.risks: Compatibility surface requires upstream conformance tests.

features.behavior: Can put the server into a sleep state after a configured idle interval while preserving health access.
features.target_overlap: Useful for large UMA models sharing a workstation.
features.rationale: Keep target-native behavior; define how persistent caches and router children behave across sleep/wake.
features.risks: Wake latency and stale device state.

features.feature: Reasoning parsing, budget, and history controls
features.behavior: Supports reasoning mode selection, token budgets, and optional preservation of reasoning in prior assistant messages.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX serves agent/reasoning models but target templates may be newer.
features.rationale: Use target-native reasoning controls and keep cache keys sensitive to template kwargs.
features.risks: Changing preservation or template behavior changes tokens and invalidates cached state.

features.behavior: Constrains output with a grammar or generated grammar derived from JSON Schema.
features.target_overlap: Useful for structured agent outputs independent of cache port.
features.rationale: Keep target-native implementation.
features.risks: Schema feature coverage and grammar conversion limits.

features.behavior: Can host a configurable Web UI alongside the API.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX can use the inherited UI for local evaluation.
features.rationale: Keep target-native UI; do not expose administrative/cache controls without authorization.
features.risks: UI, API, proxy, and tool features share one trust boundary.

features.behavior: Can estimate device requirements and adjust unset launch parameters, including context and offload, toward a target memory margin.
features.target_overlap: Highly relevant to Strix Halo UMA and multiple ROCmFPX quant formats.
features.rationale: Retain target-native estimator and teach it persistent cache/RAM reservation costs.
features.risks: Estimator errors can overcommit unified memory.

features.behavior: Routes multimodal and audio requests only when the loaded model and projector advertise the required modalities.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX may quantize multimodal-capable models.
features.rationale: Keep target-native capability detection; exclude multimodal state from persistence until identity/serialization is proven.
features.risks: Media content and projector versions affect cache compatibility.

features.behavior: Supports draft-model and n-gram speculative decoding modes and reports acceptance statistics.
features.target_overlap: ROCmFPX has stateful MTP and speculative execution.
features.rationale: Retain target-native MTP/speculation and preserve exact-boundary cache rules.
features.risks: Draft/MTP state ABI changes must invalidate persistent checkpoints.
